question: A metallic bar of Young's modulus, $0.5 \times 10^{11}\ \text{N m}^{-2}$ and coefficient of linear thermal expansion $10^{-5}\ °\text{C}^{-1}$, length $1$ m and area of cross-section $10^{-3}\ \text{m}^2$ is heated from $0°$C to $100°$C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
solution:
The bar is prevented from expanding, so the thermal strain $\alpha\Delta T$ is cancelled by an equal compressive strain.

$$F = YA\alpha\Delta T = 0.5 \times 10^{11} \times 10^{-3} \times 10^{-5} \times 100 = 5 \times 10^4\ \text{N} = 50 \times 10^3\ \text{N}$$

(The length of the bar does not matter.)
